title: We built a cutscene engine in three.js with AI and used it to shoot a 13-minute puppet horror story
author: Slackluster
selftext:
This is Episode 4 of Almost Television, a weekly puppet show we make with a lot of AI. This one is a single 13-minute story, The Monkey's Paw but with a cat, and it plays a lot like a long game cutscene, so I thought this sub might like how it works.

No video generator anywhere. The puppets, the room, the rain on the window and the fire are all built in code, in a three.js engine we wrote with Claude. Each scene is a JSON script of lines and actions: walk to the door, sit in that chair, take a bite of toast, throw the paw in the fire. The engine compiles that into a timeline and every frame is a function of time, so it can jump to any moment and render frame by frame. A camera director picks the shot for each line, the mouths follow the voice clips, and the legs are a small verlet physics sim so the feet plant as they walk.

For the final video each frame is drawn 16 times and the shadows are ray traced (three-mesh-bvh), about a second a frame, so the whole episode renders overnight in the browser.

Claude writes and directs it with us, ElevenLabs does the voices and Suno the closing song. Happy to answer anything about the engine.

[https://youtu.be/EcyNmu05fjA](https://youtu.be/EcyNmu05fjA)
